questions.question: What is the capital of France?
questions.hint: It is also known as the City of Light.

questions.question: Which is the longest river in the world?
questions.hint: It flows through Egypt.

questions.question: What is the largest desert on Earth?
questions.hint: It is surprisingly not a hot one.

questions.question: Which country spans the most time zones?
questions.hint: Think of a country with lots of overseas territories.
questions.solution: France (12 time zones with its overseas territories)

questions.question: What is the smallest country in the world by area?
questions.hint: It is located entirely inside a city.

questions.question: In which year did World War II end?
questions.hint: It is the same year the atomic bombs were dropped.

questions.question: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.hint: One small step for man...

questions.question: Julius Caesar was a famous leader of which ancient civilization?
questions.hint: It was centered on Rome.

questions.question: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
questions.hint: Near the end of the 1980s.

questions.question: Which civilization built the mountain city of Machu Picchu?
questions.hint: Their empire was in South America.

questions.question: Which gas do plants absorb from the atmosphere?
questions.hint: Humans exhale it.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.hint: It comes from the Latin word 'aurum'.

questions.question: How many bones are in the adult human body?
questions.hint: It is 200 plus six.

questions.question: What is the hardest naturally occurring substance on Earth?
questions.hint: It is allegedly a girl's best friend.

questions.question: Which planet is famous for its prominent ring system?
questions.hint: It is the sixth planet from the Sun.

questions.question: How many players from one team are on the field in a soccer match?
questions.hint: Including the goalkeeper.

questions.question: In which sport would you perform a slam dunk?
questions.hint: Michael Jordan was famous for it.

questions.question: How often are the Summer Olympic Games held?
questions.hint: It is a four-year cycle.

questions.question: What is the maximum score in a game of ten-pin bowling?
questions.hint: It requires twelve strikes in a row.

questions.question: In tennis, what is the term for a score of zero?
questions.hint: It sounds like an egg.

questions.question: Which fruit is the main ingredient of guacamole?
questions.hint: It is also called an alligator pear.

questions.question: Sushi originated in which country?
questions.hint: Its flag features a red circle.

questions.question: Which spice is the most expensive in the world by weight?
questions.hint: It is harvested from crocus flowers.

questions.question: Which pasta's name literally means 'little worms' in Italian?
questions.hint: It is long and thin.

questions.question: What is the main ingredient of traditional marzipan?
questions.hint: It is technically the seed of a stone fruit.
